beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Here is a number with four fours in it: four thousand, four hundred forty-four.

do.text: Ten times the place to its right
Are the four 4s in 4,444 worth the same?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Four fours? They're all fours. They must be worth the same.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Not quite! Each four is worth ten times the four on its right. Let's watch why.

do.text: Each place is ten times the place to its right.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Take one single four, and put it in the ones place.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Slide it one place to the left. A zero follows it in, to hold the ones place. Now it is worth forty. Ten times as much.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Again! One more place to the left, and it is worth four hundred. Ten times as much again.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: And again. Now it is worth four thousand. Ten times as much, once more.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Forty thousand. Four hundred thousand. Ten times, and ten times again.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: It is the very same four! But it is worth more every time it moves left.

do.text: The same 4, worth more at each step left.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Now slide it back, one place to the right. The four is worth ten times less.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Same four, every time. The place is what gives it its worth.

do.text: The place gives the digit its worth.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Why ten times? Let's see it with blocks. Here are nine tens, and ten ones.

do.text: What happens when ten of a small piece come together?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten ones squeeze together into one ten.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: And now there are ten tens!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten tens squeeze together into one hundred.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten of one piece always make one of the next. That is why each place is worth ten times the place to its right.

do.text: 10 of one piece make 1 of the next.
So a place is worth 10 times the place to its right.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Back to four, four, four, four. Now we can say what each four is worth.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The four in the ones place is worth four. In the tens place, forty. In the hundreds place, four hundred. In the thousands place, four thousand.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Look at the neighbors. From four up to forty, ten times. Up to four hundred, ten times again. Up to four thousand, ten times again.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So how much more is the thousands four than the tens four?

do.text: The thousands 4 compared with the tens 4: how many times as much?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two steps, ten times and then ten times again. Ten times ten is a hundred. Four thousand is one hundred times as much as forty.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: And from the ones four, all the way to the thousands four, it is three steps. Ten times ten times ten: one thousand times as much.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Now a bigger number: three hundred sixty-two thousand, five hundred eighteen. What is the six worth?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Find its place. Second from the left: the ten thousands place. Six ten thousands is sixty thousand.

do.text: Second place from the left: ten thousands.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Every digit works the same way: the digit times its place. Add them all up. Three hundred thousand, plus sixty thousand, plus two thousand, plus five hundred, plus ten, plus eight.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: To read a big number, split it into groups of three digits at the comma. The first group is three hundred sixty-two, and we say thousand after it. The second group is five hundred eighteen.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three hundred sixty-two thousand, five hundred eighteen. Say each group, and name its place.

do.text: three hundred sixty-two thousand, five hundred eighteen

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Zeros need care. Let's write three hundred five thousand, seventy.

do.text: Write three hundred five thousand, seventy as a numeral.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three hundred five thousand fills the first group: three, zero, five.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Now seventy. The second group needs three digits: no hundreds, seven tens, no ones.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So the zeros are holding places. What if I leave one out?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Then the three slips one place to the right, and it is worth ten times less. That is thirty-five thousand, seventy. A different number!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Which is greater: forty-eight thousand, seven hundred twenty-nine, or forty-eight thousand, seven hundred ninety-two? Line the numbers up, place under place.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Start at the left, where the places are biggest. Four ten thousands and four ten thousands: the same. Eight thousands, eight thousands: the same. Seven hundreds, seven hundreds: the same.

do.text: Compare from the left, place by place.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Tens. Two tens against nine tens. Nine tens is more, so the second number is greater.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: But the first number ends in a nine, and the second ends in a two!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Nine ones is only nine. Nine tens is ninety. The first place that is different decides, so the ones never get a vote.

do.text: The first place that differs decides.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Now put three numbers in order, least to greatest. We add forty-eight thousand, two hundred seventy-nine.

do.text: Least is the smallest; greatest is the largest.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Same plan. Ten thousands, thousands: all the same. Hundreds: seven, seven, and two. Two hundreds is the least, so this number comes first.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: And we already know the other two: seven twenty-nine comes before seven ninety-two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Now rounding. Round forty-eight thousand, seven hundred twenty-nine to the nearest thousand.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: It lies between two thousands: forty-eight thousand, and forty-nine thousand. Each little tick is one hundred.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Seven ticks along is forty-eight thousand, seven hundred. Twenty-nine more, and here is our number.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Which thousand is it closer to? Find the halfway mark: forty-eight thousand, five hundred.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Our number is past halfway, so it rounds up to forty-nine thousand.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Can I do it without the line?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Yes. Look at the digit just right of the thousands place. It is a seven. Five or more rounds up. Four or less stays.

do.text: Look right of the rounding place: 7.
5 or more: round up. 4 or less: stay.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One last kind of question: find a number in between two others.

do.text: Which number is more than 48,729 and less than 48,792?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: More than forty-eight thousand, seven hundred twenty-nine, and less than forty-eight thousand, seven hundred ninety-two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Zoom in on the line. Each tick is ten. The numbers we want live in the gap between the two marks.

do.text: The answer lives in the gap.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Try forty-eight thousand, seven hundred fifteen. Same hundreds, but one ten is less than two tens. It lands before the gap. Too small.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Try seven ninety-five. Nine tens, same as the top. Then five ones is more than two ones. Past the gap. Too big.

do.text: Try 48,795: 9 tens = 9 tens, but 5 ones > 2 ones.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Now seven fifty. Five tens is more than two tens, and less than nine tens. Inside the gap. That is the one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Let's end where we began, with four, four, four, four.

do.text: Ten times the place to its right

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Now I can see it. Four, forty, four hundred, four thousand.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each is ten times the one on its right.

do.text: Each place is ten times the place to its right.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: That one fact reads a number, writes it, compares it, and rounds it, however long it is.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The place gives the digit its value. One place to the left is ten times as much.
